page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / The brainstorm
title: The brainstorm
description:
Tom, Anna and Denise get together to share their ideas about Tip Top Trading's upcoming launch, but they can't agree on things! Anna's ideas are met with some negative comments and she has to learn how to disagree with the other's viewpoint in a confident but polite manner.
This episode explores language to use when you want to disagree with somebody else's ideas and put forward your viewpoint..
phrases: Well, I'm not so sure about that...
I see your point but I actually think...

listening_challenge.question: What discount does Anna suggest giving to their clients who order the Imperial Lemons?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Welcome! The team at Tip Top Trading are hard at work, making plans for the launch and presentation of their latest product: the revolutionary, almost real Imperial Lemon. They are 'brainstorming', sharing ideas on how to make their lemon a success.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: But it needs to be bright!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: This is much more exciting.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: But having three colours would work better.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: There is a lot of disagreement going on, which is putting Anna's vocabulary to the test!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Right, I'm taking the final decision: the colour scheme will be green and yellow, so that's that. Now, the first presentation will be to er, Mr, er, Slime.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Mr Lime.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh, er, Mr Lime - that bit of biscuit looked like an 's' – Mr Lime, thank you Annabel.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Anna.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Mr Lime and his team at Citrus Ventures. Ideas please!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Why don't we offer Citrus Ventures a special opening offer: 20% off Imperial Lemon orders made this month.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Hmm...

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: We could even do that for all our regular clients.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: That would be a big risk.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: If we do that once, all our clients will start asking for 20% off everything.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No, I disagree.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: We'll be bankrupt!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No, you're wrong.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Er- Anna, maybe you should find a better way of saying you disagree with Denise.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'm so frustrated! I can't think of the right words.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
It helps if you try phrases like: 
Well, I'm not so sure about that... then explain why. 
Or start your sentence with 'but' when you want to disagree with what has just been said. 
Or, to seem more polite, you can try: 
I see your point, but actually I think...

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'll try.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: And don't be aggressive Anna - and give your reasons too, or you'll upset Denise again!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK. Well, I'm not so sure about that. I think it will improve our sales of lemons and make our clients happy. Happy clients will come back to buy more.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes, that's a good point Annabe - Anna.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: But 20% is a lot – maybe 5% would be better.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But if we're going to make a special offer, we should make it so good that everyone will say yes!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: But people might think there's something wrong with our lemons and that we're desperate to get rid of them.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I see your point, but, if we explain this is just a special offer for special clients, they'll understand.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: I like that idea. Good: 20% off for all regular clients just for this month. Anna, you'll be making the presentation to Citrus Ventures, so make sure you include that offer.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Uh-huh.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Right, next, what photos do we have of the lemons...?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Finding the right words to disagree in meetings isn't always easy, but Anna managed in the end. She started sentences with this short word to show that she was about to disagree with what had just been said:

The next big challenge for Anna will be her presentation to Citrus Ventures. Join us again soon to find out what happens!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I've got to do a good job but it's going to take me ages. Ah well, I had better get started otherwise I'm going to be here all night!
